pr.title: Add LLVM realtime sanitizer
pr.description:
This is a new attempt at adding the [LLVM real-time sanitizer](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/RealtimeSanitizer.html) to rust.

Previously this was attempted in https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/3766.

Since then the `sanitize` attribute was introduced in https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/142681 and it is a lot more flexible than the old `no_santize` attribute. This allows adding real-time sanitizer without the need for a new attribute, like it was proposed in the RFC. Because i only add a new value to a existing command line flag and to a attribute i don't think an MCP is necessary.

Currently real-time santizer is usable in rust code with the [rtsan-standalone](https://crates.io/crates/rtsan-standalone) crate. This downloads or builds the sanitizer runtime and then links it into the rust binary.

The first commit adds support for more detailed sanitizer information.
The second commit then actually adds real-time sanitizer.
The third adds a warning against using real-time sanitizer with async functions, cloures and blocks because it doesn't behave as expected when used with async functions. I am not sure if this is actually wanted, so i kept it in a seperate commit.
The fourth commit adds the documentation for real-time sanitizer.
pr.author: inkreasing

analysis.summary: The MIR inliner must compare the complete sanitizer function attributes of caller and callee, not just the disabled-sanitizer bit set. This PR adds LLVM RealtimeSanitizer support, introducing RtsanSetting (Nonblocking/Blocking/Caller) alongside the existing disabled sanitizer set, and consequently widens the inline compatibility gate and the inline(always) warning to the full SanitizerFnAttrs. This is a feature-addition PR, not a confirmed historical bug fix; the reusable invariant concerns inline/force-inline legality.
analysis.originalLogic: In compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/inline.rs, check_codegen_attributes obtains the caller's codegen attributes from the caller's DefId and rejects the inline candidate when the caller's and callee's `no_sanitize` sets differ: `if callee_attrs.no_sanitize != codegen_fn_attrs.no_sanitize { return Err("incompatible sanitizer set"); }`. Separately, the `inline(always)` diagnostic fires only when `!codegen_fn_attrs.no_sanitize.is_empty()` and warns "setting `sanitize` off will have no effect after inlining".
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Comparing only the disabled-sanitizer subset (the old `no_sanitize: SanitizerSet`) instead of the complete sanitizer settings. Under that comparison, a caller and callee with identical disabled bits but different `rtsan_setting` values (e.g. caller Caller/default, callee Nonblocking or Blocking) are treated as compatible, so the callee can be inlined and its runtime sanitizer context boundary is lost. Correspondingly, an `inline(always)` check that only tests whether the disabled set is non-empty fails to warn when the only non-default setting is the realtime mode. The corrected transformation compares full `SanitizerFnAttrs` (disabled set plus `rtsan_setting`) and warns whenever `sanitizers != SanitizerFnAttrs::default()`.
analysis.inputDomain: Pairs of Rust functions where the caller and callee have identical disabled-sanitizer bits but different `#[sanitize(realtime = "...")]` modes, or where an `#[inline(always)]` function has only a non-default realtime mode. Realtime modes are Nonblocking, Blocking, and the default Caller; the realtime sanitizer is enabled with `-Zsanitizer=realtime`. The attribute may also be inherited from an enclosing item, and may appear on async fns, async blocks, and async closures.
analysis.trigger: The inline pass evaluates a callee whose full sanitizer attributes differ from the caller's while their disabled-sanitizer bit sets are equal, specifically because `rtsan_setting` differs; or a force-inlined function has a non-default sanitize setting such as `realtime = "nonblocking"`.
preconditions: Sanitizer instrumentation decisions are function-granular, as stated in the sanitizer documentation.
The callee and caller are otherwise eligible for MIR inlining.
The realtime setting can be Nonblocking, Blocking, or the default Caller.
The inliner's attribute check is reached before the call is inlined.
For the lint path, the function requests `#[inline(always)]` and has a non-default sanitize setting.
pitfalls: Equating sanitizer compatibility with equality of the disabled-sanitizer set alone; realtime mode is a separate setting that changes instrumentation context.

Assuming the default Caller mode is the same as an explicit `realtime = "caller"`; both are the semantic default for the attribute comparison, but a missing attribute must not be confused with a missing disabled set.
Forgetting that `#[inline(always)]` can make sanitize settings ineffective; the warning condition must include any non-default sanitize setting, not just non-empty disabled bits.
Checking only the function on which the attribute is written and ignoring sanitizer-setting inheritance from enclosing defs.
Treating the async-only rtsan_nonblocking_async lint as evidence about inlining legality; it is a separate diagnostic about executor behavior.
analysis.testStrategy: Use compile-time UI tests rather than claiming sanitizer execution. Construct two programs differing only in the callee's `#[sanitize(realtime = ...)]` value (same disabled set), with a caller in another realtime mode, and verify the inliner refuses the cross-setting inline (e.g. inspect optimized MIR or the resulting codegen/symbol structure) while allowing the equal-setting case. Add a focused `inline(always)` UI test where the only non-default attribute is `realtime = "nonblocking"` and assert the widened warning text "non-default `sanitize` will have no effect after inlining". Also test malformed realtime values (`on`, `off`) produce E0539 listing `nonblocking`, `blocking`, `caller`, and test attribute inheritance. Runtime rtsan tests require `//@ needs-sanitizer-realtime`, `-Z sanitizer=realtime`, and `RTSAN_OPTIONS=abort_on_error=0`; they are integration checks, not evidence that this patch was executed here.
evidence: lint.primary_message("non-default `sanitize` will have no effect after inlining");
function again the program will get sanitized.
